Twelve AI models launched in a single week. That is not hype — that is a structural shift in how enterprises need to think about AI.

GPT-5.4 shipped with three variants. Grok 4.20 claimed the lowest hallucination rate at the frontier. Google released Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite. Mistral dropped Small 4. Seven more models covered code, image, audio, and multimodal capabilities.

Here is the real takeaway: frontier model performance has converged so tightly that the GDPVal benchmark — testing AI against human professionals across 44 occupations — shows top models scoring 83%, matching or exceeding human experts in areas like financial modeling.

The "best" model is no longer a simple answer. It depends on the task, the cost tolerance, the latency requirement, and the domain. The companies getting real results are not picking one model and hoping for the best. They are building orchestration layers that route work to the right model dynamically.

If switching AI providers in your stack takes months instead of hours, your architecture is already a liability.
